text:
alex: heads up — ran the long-context generation stress on ded. Seeing steady GPU memory growth that never comes down on A100 jobs. Repro script attached below. :sad_panda:

maria: oh no, how big is the growth?

alex: ~500MB per 10k tokens, linear over time. After ~1M tokens the process OOMs if left long enough. H100 runs look better, only small spikes then stable.

jing: interesting. did you enable kvcache paging? could be eviction not freeing page table entries.

alex: yes REDWOOD_KVCACHE=1. I added kvcache debug logs: shows page_alloc_count >> page_free_count. snippet:

```

kvcache: page_alloc_count=41234
kvcache: page_free_count=40120
kvcache: live_pages=1114
kvcache: page_table_entries=8192
kvcache: evict_scan_hits=980
kvcache: evict_scan_misses=487

```

alex: evict_scan_misses are suspiciously high. The allocator is handing out pages but free path seems to fail ~1% of the time and that accumulates.

sam: can you paste the eviction path logs? also which driver versions on A100/H100?

alex: A100: CUDA 11.8, NVIDIA driver 525. H100: CUDA 12.x, driver 535. Evict logs: 

```

[evict] page 0x7f8c3b000 freed -> marked for reclaim
[evict] page 0x7f8c3b000 queued to GPU_free_list
[evict] page 0x7f8c3b000 removed from owner_map
[evict] owner_map_lookup failed for 0x7f8c3b000 (already null) -> skipping physical_free

```

alex: that "already null" is our clue. The page gets cleared from owner_map earlier but still enqueued for physical_free. On A100 the physical free path sometimes does nothing because the GPU-side buffer refcount didn't decrement. On H100 the ordering seems to avoid the race.

maria: do we have any atomic/unlock ordering differences in our page table code paths? page removal should be atomic with dequeuing.

jing: I dug in. There's an unprotected code path in pagetable::evict_one where we do: 

```
if (owner_map.erase(page_id)) {
  enqueue_gpu_free(page);
}
```

and enqueue_gpu_free() posts a work item that later calls gpu_free(page) which does an attempt to clear owner_map again in some fallback handling. If race runs the other way we hit the "already null" branch and skip physical_free.

jing: on H100 the gpu_free work tends to run before the fallback because of different async copy scheduling; on A100 the worker thread ordering sometimes reverses. So it's a classic double-check-then-act race.

sam: can we make erase+enqueue one atomic operation? like return the removed pointer and only enqueue if non-null, and ensure gpu_free doesn't re-check owner_map but uses the returned pointer.

alex: patched a quick fix locally: 

```
// old
bool removed = owner_map.erase(page_id);
if (removed) enqueue_gpu_free(page);

// new
Page* removed_ptr = owner_map.remove_and_return(page_id); // atomic
if (removed_ptr) {
  enqueue_gpu_free_direct(removed_ptr);
}
```

alex: quick stress run with fix looks promising: freed pages match allocs now in debug output. A100 memory growth flattened.

maria: nice. we'll need a proper API change for owner_map to expose remove_and_return and audit all callsites. Also add asserts to gpu_free to avoid double-free.

perf-bot: perf alert: after patch, 1h generation test decreased PCIe memcpy count by 22% on A100 and avg tail latency improved 8%.

jing: also saw that our page table hash size interacts with slotmap fragmentation. If owner_map lookup uses 32-bit keys on 64-bit pointers we could get collisions that caused entries to be left dangling. Not sure if that contributed here but worth checking.

sam: good call — add CI test that runs with 32k unique pages across mixed evict/insert workload to catch collisions.

alex: repro command I used: 

```
# run long-context stress on ded pool
ENV_REDWOOD_KVCACHE=1 REDWOOD_KVCACHE_DEBUG=1 ./run_infer.sh --model redwood-open-xxl --tokens 1000000 --dedicated
```

alex: logs + nvprof trace attached to thread (uploaded). nvprof summary on A100 before fix: dozens of small cudaMemcpyAsync host->device calls per token; after fix they batch better.

maria: is batching impacted by leftover page refs? maybe many tiny frees forced synchronizations.

jing: yes, we saw extra stream synchronizations when worker retried gpu_free fallback. That killed batching and caused PCIe thrash.

sam: next steps: 1) PR with owner_map remove_and_return + enqueue change, 2) add assert in gpu_free to crash in CI if double-free detected, 3) add long-context kvcache stress to perf-regressions, 4) run on A100/H100 matrix.

alex: I'll open the PR and tag eng-runtime + eng-ml for test runs. Patch is small but risky so want canary deploy.

maria: thanks — add metrics to console: kvcache.live_pages, evict_misses, gpu_free_retry_count. We can chart them per model.

jing: also file a follow-up: audit any fallback paths that re-check owner_map; we should move to a single owner semantics to avoid future double-check races.

alex: cool. I'll post PR link and attach the nvprof captures. If anyone wants to repro locally I can share the stress runner. :thumbsup:

perf-bot: regression test queued: long_context_kvcache_stress (A100) — keep an eye on task 3421.

sam: great work catching the cross-gpu ordering race — could have been subtle in prod. :eyes:
